reason: The cited evidence does not directly support the key premises. E1 attributes wear resistance to a nanohierarchical architecture and multi-type adaptive interfaces, not a uniform oxide film. E2 discusses high-temperature strength plateaus unrelated to wear or oxidation. E3 merely notes oxidative wear occurred, without establishing a protective, self-lubricating oxide layer that governs performance. The premises are thus largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: In-situ oxide film formation governs HEA wear performance
Oxide film is continuous, mechanically robust, and self-lubricating
Oxide film forms uniformly on homogeneous HEA coatings in oxidizing environments
Oxide film reduces direct metal contact and redistributes contact stresses
Suppressing oxide formation (inert atmosphere) will worsen wear resistance
